name: Archaeological Museum
hero_subtitle: Key Tetouan landmark — scale, silence and the logistics of an imperial city.

overview.title: Where the empire stored its strength
overview.p1: The Archaeological Museum is one of Tetouan's most striking stops: long vaulted halls built to store grain and house huge numbers of horses. The architecture is about capacity and climate control more than decoration — thick walls, dark passages and a sense of organised power.
overview.p2: Walk the full length of the halls, let your eyes adjust, and notice how much cooler it is inside than on the plateau outside. The site is less about one showpiece façade and more about understanding how Tetouan fed and supplied itself.
overview.p3: Come in the morning in summer. Combine with the memorial or return to the main square later. A guide helps with dates and numbers; the place itself already speaks of scale.

food.title: Eat after the halls
food.p1: Little food is available on site. Plan lunch toward the medina or Ville Nouvelle after your visit.
food.li2: Lunch in the medina after the taxi back
food.li3: Only a light snack if you come straight from the memorial
food.li4: Coffee in Ville Nouvelle if heading to the station afterward
food.li5: Do not leave food waste on the historic site
food.p2: Carry water onto the site. Dry air and walking increase thirst even inside the vaults.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Archaeological Museum

1.title: Morning slot in hot months
1.desc: Plateau sun is strong by late morning. Aim for opening time, finish the halls before midday, and keep the afternoon for shaded medina lanes or a museum.

2.title: Wear proper walking shoes
2.desc: Floors are uneven in places. Comfortable shoes matter more than looks. A small torch is rarely needed, but some corners are dark.

3.title: Taxi there, walk later if you want
3.desc: Save energy for the halls. A petit taxi from the main square is cheap; agree the fare first or use the meter where it is used.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: Yes — it is a ticketed historic site. Keep small change or a card if accepted at the desk.

q2.question: How long should I stay?
q2.answer: Forty-five to ninety minutes covers the main halls without rushing.

q3.question: Is it suitable in summer?
q3.answer: The interior is cooler than outside, but the approach can be hot. Morning is best.

q4.question: Do I need a guide?
q4.answer: Not required. A guide adds dates and context; the architecture is readable on its own.

q5.question: How far from the main square?
q5.answer: A short taxi ride or a longer walk in heat. Most visitors take a petit taxi.
